question: Ketan bought a shirt and sold it to Mahesh at a profit of 5%. Mahesh sold it to David at a loss of 24%. If David paid ₹3990, then the cost price (in ₹) of the shirt Ketan bought is
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the fractional multiplier method for successive profit and loss:

Initial CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 × (100 − L%) ÷ 100 = Final SP

⇒ CP × 105/100 × 76/100 = 3990

⇒ CP × 21/20 × 19/25 = 3990

⇒ CP × 399/500 = 3990

⇒ CP = 3990 × 500 ÷ 399 = 5000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit percentage of Ketan = 5%

Loss percentage of Mahesh = 24%

Price paid by David = ₹3990

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 − Loss% ÷ 100)
